To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the planned objectives for the forestry and the wood-processing industries in northern Vietnam cannot be achieved in 2010-2015. The main reasons are that the planned levels of production are not financially viable for the stakeholders,

government objectives for the forestry and timber industries in northern Vietnam cannot be achieved in 2010-2015, but the objectives could be achieved in 2030 if the Government of Vietnam implements the proposed policy scenarios.
The Government of Vietnam's objectives for the forestry and the wood-processing industries are not achievable in the 2015 planning period.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a spatial equilibrium model to analyse policies for the forestry and the wood-processing industries.
the economic feasibility of government plans, and the results of our analysis provide a basis for policy makers to consider alternative policy scenarios.

the development of a spatial equilibrium model with the objective of determining the optimal levels of prices and supply and demand quantities for the forestry and processing industries in northern Vietnam.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Government of Northern Vietnam has set too many objectives, and that some of them should be reduced.
the government should revise the plan for the forestry and the wood-processing industries for 2011-15.

the Government of northern Vietnam should reduce the number of new wood-processing factories and increase the design production capacity in the new factories to achieve economies of scale and international market competitiveness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a policy scenario that is more consistent with market forces would lead to a better economic outcome.
a more realistic policy is needed to achieve the national objectives for the forestry and the wood-processing industries.

, in the context of the northern region, the government should not only focus on increasing the area of planted forest and the production capacity of new wood-processing factories but also on improving the quality of planted forest and wood-processing products, which will increase the competitiveness of the wood-processing industries and the value of planted forest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a spatial equilibrium model can be used to assess the feasibility of the Government of Vietnam's forestry and wood-processing policies.

a policy of price control is not an appropriate policy instrument for the wood-processing industry, and the government should consider other instruments, such as tax incentives for investment and technology development.

policy makers and stakeholders should be more realistic in setting objectives for forestry and the wood-processing industries, and they should be more aware of the need to achieve financial viability and sustainability.
